ai.description: Ghate's Shrub Frog is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brown, mottled dorsum and pale cream belly. It is distinguished by a prominent white spot on the snout and granular skin texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes ghatei* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-colored X-shaped marking on its dorsum, which is absent in most similar shrub frog species.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes ghatei* inhabits the high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the northern Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Ghate's Shrub Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden within dense vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects on leaves.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes ghatei* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in leaf litter or tree hollows.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes ghatei* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes ghatei* consists of a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in mid-elevation evergreen forests.
